Anypoint Exchange Release Notes

Anypoint Exchange is a curated catalog of reusable assets such as agents, APIs, API groups, API spec fragments, brokers, custom assets, examples, large language models (LLMs), Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, policies, templates, integration assets such as connectors. You can catalog (publish), share, discover, learn about, and reuse assets within your organization to facilitate collaboration, boost productivity, and promote standards.

November 9, 2026

What’s New

  • You can now add a scanner to discover, import, and sync agents from Microsoft 365 Copilot into Exchange. The scanner imports agents created in Microsoft 365 Copilot Agent Builder. After the agents are in Exchange, you can govern them and consume them in other applications.

    For more information, see Adding a Scanner for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

October 21, 2026

What’s New

  • Exchange now supports OpenAPI Specification (OAS) 3.1. You can upload OAS 3.1 API specifications in YAML or JSON format, publish them as REST API assets, and view the specification documentation. Exchange generates a RAML version of each OAS 3.1 asset. When you download an OAS 3.1 asset as OAS, you get the original OAS 3.1 specification.

    Exchange doesn’t resolve dynamic references ($dynamicRef and $dynamicAnchor) and doesn’t apply custom $schema dialects in OAS 3.1 API specifications.

October 14, 2026

What’s New

  • You can now add a scanner to discover, import, and sync MCP servers from Kong Gateway into Exchange. After the MCP servers are in Exchange, you can govern them and consume them in other applications.

    For more information, see Adding a Scanner for Kong MCP Server.

  • You can now add a scanner to discover, import, and sync agents from ServiceNow AI Agents into Exchange. The scanner imports agents created in ServiceNow AI Agent Studio. After the agents are in Exchange, you can govern them and consume them in other applications.

    For more information, see Adding a Scanner for ServiceNow AI Agents.

  • You can now make your MCP server and agent assets public in Exchange, the same way you do for API assets. Exchange administrators can publish an asset version to the organization’s public portal from the Share dialog, and set instance visibility to public or private. The asset stays available inside your organization. Consumers can then add public MCP servers to API Manager. See, see, Adding an MCP Server from Public Exchange.

    For more information, see Publishing an Asset to a Public Portal.

September 4, 2026

What’s New

  • When the scanner discovers an API in Kong Gateway, it assigns an asset type in Exchange based on the API’s Kong protocol and plugins.

    For more information, see Protocol to Asset Type Mapping.

Fixed Issues

Issue Resolution ID

Agent retrieval response times are now faster.

W-21922690

The Kong API Gateway scanner no longer publishes the same asset as new on every scan run.

W-23420989

The Microsoft Azure AI Foundry scanner now captures the full agent responses endpoint URL instead of the project URL.

W-23542862

The Snowflake scanner now includes Comment and Profile in metadata fields.

W-23599680

August 28, 2026

What’s New

  • The Kong Gateway scanner now detects gRPC and GraphQL protocols and assigns the correct asset type in Exchange and Omni Gateway for these APIs. APIs that use other protocols are registered as asset type REST for now. MuleSoft plans to support more protocols in a future release.

    For more information, see Adding a Scanner for Kong Gateway.

  • Agent scanners now deliver a consistent set of metadata across every provider. Whether you scan Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Copilot, Google Vertex, Snowflake, Databricks, or GoDaddy ANS, each scanner captures the same core fields for agent identity, lifecycle and ownership, and the agent’s model and instructions. This gives you a uniform view of each agent, where it lives, and what powers it, regardless of the platform it runs on. Standardized metadata makes it easier to compare, govern, and discover agents from different providers in one place.

August 10, 2026

Fixed Issues

Issue Resolution ID

Agent retrieval response times are now faster.

W-21922690

The Kong Gateway scanner no longer publishes the same asset as new on every scan run.

W-23420989

The Microsoft Azure AI Foundry scanner now captures the full agent responses endpoint URL instead of the project URL.

W-23542862

The Snowflake scanner now includes Comment and Profile in metadata fields.

W-23599680

Creating and testing Databricks scanner connections now works for Databricks workspaces on Azure.

W-23255193

The list of scanner providers now displays a complete list of providers.

W-23432675

Agent scanners can now be deleted from the Scanners page.

W-23464071

Creating an Amazon Bedrock agent scanner no longer fails.

W-23464715

August 6, 2026

What’s New

  • API scanners now read policies from these provider platforms: Amazon API Gateway, Google Apigee, Azure API Management, and Kong Gateway.

    For more information, see:

    • Adding a Scanner for Amazon API Gateway

    • Adding a Scanner for Google Apigee

    • Adding a Scanner for Azure API Management

    • Adding a Scanner for Kong Gateway

July 2026

What’s New

  • Publishing custom connectors and Mule plugins to Exchange now requires Java compatibility metadata in mule-artifact.json for new versions that change supported Java compatibility.

    To avoid publishing failures, update your connector build configuration to a supported supported Mule SDK or plugin configuration that writes Java compatibility metadata before publishing new versions.

    This change doesn’t affect connectors already published to Exchange or running applications.

    For configuration steps and troubleshooting, see Publishing Connectors to Exchange.

  • Exchange now supports publishing A2A Protocol v1.0 agent cards. When you create an agent asset, you can select A2A v1.0 card as the protocol type to publish a v1.0-compliant Agent Card. The v1.0 card supports the supportedInterfaces field for declaring transport bindings and optional card signatures.

    A2A v0.3 cards remain available as a separate protocol option (A2A v0.3 card). A single asset version can carry both a v0.3 card and a v1.0 card under separate classifiers. There is no automatic conversion between versions.

    For more information, see Create an Agent.

  • The card details page for A2A v1.0 agents now displays:

    • Supported interfaces (protocol binding, URL, protocol version, and tenant)

    • Signature indicator (shown only for signed cards)

    • Provider information

    • Security schemes

    • Capabilities (streaming, push notifications, state transition history)

    • Skills (with descriptions, input/output modes, and examples)

  • Exchange now includes Agent Network as a supported asset type. An agent network is a coordinated group of agents, brokers, LLMs, and MCP servers that acts as a central hub for defining, validating, and executing agentic processes across your enterprise. This asset is published to Exchange from Anypoint Code Builder and is read-only.

    For more information, see Asset Types.

  • You can now use the Agentforce scanner to import Agentforce agents into Exchange.

    For more information, see Adding a Scanner for Salesforce Agentforce Agents.

  • You can now add scanners to automatically discover and catalog MCP servers from these external providers:

    • Microsoft Azure API Management MCP Server

    • Databricks Agent Bricks MCP Server

      For more information, see:

      • Adding a Scanner for Salesforce Agentforce Agents

      • Adding a Scanner for Azure API Management MCP Server

      • Adding a Scanner for Databricks MCP Server

  • The Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime scanner now adds richer metadata to Exchange agent cards and documentation, helping users evaluate agents faster.

    The Exchange details page for scanned agents now shows:

    • Created At

    • Updated At

    • Foundation Model

    • Skills

    • Collaboration Model

  • Importing Agentforce agents from Settings is deprecated. To import Agentforce agents, create an Agentforce scanner.

    For more information, see Adding a Scanner for Salesforce Agentforce Agents.

Fixed Issues

Issue Resolution ID

The Databricks scanner now correctly authenticates on Azure-hosted Databricks workspaces using OAuth Machine-to-Machine (M2M) authentication and no longer returns an invalid_client error.

W-23255193

When a new scheduled scanner run starts, any existing manual run in PENDING_REVIEW status is now fully cancelled, including termination of its associated Temporal workflow, so subsequent manual runs no longer fail with a 409 conflict.

W-22735433

The Salesforce Agentforce scanner now supports non-root business groups, enabling discovery and scanning of Agentforce assets across all business groups in an organization.

W-23293582

June 2026

What’s New

The required scope URL to retrieve agent metadata for the Microsoft Copilot scanner is updated to https://<orgId>.api.crm.dynamics.com. For more information see, Adding a Scanner for Microsoft Copilot Studio.

Fixed Issues

Issue Resolution ID

The scope URL validation for the Microsoft Copilot scanner is now updated and no longer fails to retrieve agents during a scan.

W-22550680

Agent cards for agents added in Exchange from Anthropic Claude, Databricks Agent Bricks, and Snowflake Cortex AI now display the protocol type as Other instead of A2A.

W-22493536, W-22493540, and W-22493542

What’s New

  • Administrators can now add scanners to automatically discover and catalog services for these external providers:

    • Anthropic Claude (agents)

    • Databricks Agent Bricks (agents)

    • LangChain LangSmith (agents)

    • Snowflake Cortex AI (agents)

    • Snowflake MCP (MCP servers)

      For more information, see:

      • Adding a Scanner for Anthropic Claude Managed Agents

      • Adding a Scanner for Databricks Agent Bricks

      • Adding a Scanner for LangChain LangSmith

      • Adding a Scanner for Snowflake Cortex AI

      • Adding a Scanner for Snowflake MCP Server

May 2026

What’s New

  • Generative AI documentation now supports gRPC APIs, MCP servers, and agents, in addition to REST, SOAP, AsyncAPI, and GraphQL APIs.

    For more information, see Generating API Documentation with Generative AI.

  • You can now add a scanner to discover, import, and sync APIs from external providers into Exchange. Once imported, you can apply governance rulesets and publish these services to a developer portal. Supported gateways are Amazon API Gateway, Azure API Management, Kong API Gateway, and Google Apigee.

    For more information, see:

    • Adding a Scanner for Amazon API Gateway

    • Adding a Scanner for Azure API Management

    • Adding a Scanner for Kong Gateway

    • Adding a Scanner for Google Apigee

  • The Amazon AgentCore scanner has been enhanced to now support the automatic discovery and cataloging of MCP servers. After the MCP servers are registered, you can govern and consume them in other applications.

    For more information, see Adding a Scanner for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore MCP.

  • You can now review and approve scan results before they’re imported into Exchange, giving you control over which external services are added to your catalog. When you configure a scanner to Ask to review, its status changes to Pending review after the scan completes. Open the scan to choose which services to import. Services you don’t import remain pending and reappear in the next scan. To permanently exclude a service from future scans, use the action menu to add it to the Skipped list.

    To enable manual review, set the scheduled run configuration to Ask to review when you add or edit a scanner.

    For more information, see Review Scan Results Manually.

  • The Agent Scanners page in the Exchange sidebar has been renamed to Scanners, where you can now access all scanners regardless of service type from a single page.

    For more information, see Discovering and Cataloging External Services with Scanners.

April 2026

What’s New

  • Exchange now supports SHA-256 checksums for all assets, providing higher security standards for verifying asset integrity during download and distribution.

  • In addition to REST APIs, generative AI now supports expanded API documentation generation for SOAP APIs, AsyncAPI, and GraphQL. You can now generate documentation for API assets published using either single-file or multi-file specifications.

    For more information, see Generating API Documentation with Generative AI.

  • Agents verified by GoDaddy agent network service (ANS) in API Management now display a verified badge in the Exchange catalog and on asset detail pages, helping you quickly identify trusted assets. Instances also show whether managed instances are verified.

    For more information, see:

    • Agent Fabric Assets

    • View Instances

    • Configuring Instances

  • You can now add a scanner to automatically discover and catalog Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Microsoft Foundry agents. This lets you govern and consume the agents in other applications.

    For more information, see:

    • Adding a Scanner for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime

    • Adding a Scanner for Microsoft Foundry

  • Permissions for configuring a Microsoft Copilot Studio scanner now include read-only access for scanning Microsoft Copilot Studio agent metadata.

    For more information, see Adding a Scanner for Microsoft Copilot Studio.

March 2026

What’s New

  • You can now use the Exchange MCP server endpoint to retrieve asset and instance metadata from Exchange for your AI agents, without requiring Omni Gateway.

    For more information, see Retrieving Asset Metadata Using an MCP Server Endpoint.

  • Informatica’s CDGC Metadata Search MCP server and Cloud Address Verification MCP server are now available in Exchange. These assets are published to Exchange under Provided by MuleSoft and are maintained by Informatica.

    For more information about publicly hosted MCP servers, see MuleSoft Assets.

  • Exchange now supports gRPC APIs. You can now publish and consume gRPC APIs in Exchange. A gRPC API is specified in a Protocol Buffers (.proto) file that declares services and message contracts.

    For more information, see:

    • Asset Types

    • Creating an Asset

February 2026

What’s New

  • You can now add a scanner to automatically discover and register GoDaddy ANS agents. GoDaddy ANS agents are verified by GoDaddy to be safe and secure. Govern and consume the agents in other applications.

    For more information, see:

    • Discovering and Cataloging External Services with Scanners

    • Adding a Scanner for GoDaddy ANS

January 2026

What’s New

  • You can now add agent scanners to automatically discover and register AI agents across agent ecosystems on external platforms, which include Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Azure Copilot. After the agents are registered, govern and consume them in other applications.

    For more information, see Discovering and Cataloging External Services with Scanners.

  • You can now use an MCP server URL to add the server’s metadata when publishing it to the registry in Exchange.

    For more information, see Create an MCP Server.

  • Exchange now syncs public MCP servers from the official MCP registry to Provided by MuleSoft.

    These public MCP servers are maintained by the original providers and not MuleSoft.

  • You can now create and manage instances for publicly available MCP servers in API Manager to govern and monitor public assets.

    These assets are published to Exchange under Provided by MuleSoft and are maintained by their original providers, not by MuleSoft. When you create an instance from a publicly available asset, the instance is created within your private organization in Exchange and managed like any other instance in API Manager.

    For more information see, Adding an MCP Server from Public Exchange.

  • You can now request access to running instances from publicly available assets. Instances for MCP servers published in Provided by MuleSoft are created within your private organization.

November 2025

What’s New

  • API Notebook reached End of Life on November 28, 2025.

October 2025

What’s New

  • API Notebook is scheduled for End of Life on November 28, 2025.

  • Exchange now supports agent, broker, large language model (LLM), and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server asset types and Agentforce agents for Agent Fabric.

    For more information, see:

    • Agent Fabric.

    • Asset Types

    • Importing Agentforce Agents

    • Create an agent asset

    • Create an MCP server asset

    • Create an LLM asset

July 2025

What’s New

  • Admins can choose how asset owners can dte asset versions in Exchange. They can enable or disable the ability to permanently delete an asset to reuse the GAV (group ID, asset ID, and version) for a new asset. It doesn’t matter when the asset version was created. When enabled, asset owners see an option to allow the GAV to be reused when deleting an asset version. When disabled, the GAV can’t be reused after deleting the asset version.

    For more information, see Managing Asset Deletion.

  • Admins can control whether or not to assign owner roles when creating assets using a connected app. When enabled, when creating new assets using a connected app, roles aren’t assigned to connected app owners. When disabled, roles are assigned by default.

    For more information, see Managing Connected Apps.

June 2025

What’s New

  • Users can now generate comprehensive and standardized API documentation for REST APIs from Exchange. This feature uses Einstein generative AI to analyze and create documentation, saving time and effort and ensuring high quality API creation. Users can focus on developing APIs while Einstein handles the documentation.

    For more information, see Generating API Documentation with Generative AI.

  • Client application owners can now add multiple individual users or teams as additional owners, granting them management capabilities for the client application.

    For more information, see Add Users as Client Application Owners.

December 2024

What’s New

  • This product is now available on Hyperforce.

    Anypoint Platform instances on the Hyperforce infrastructure are:

    • Canada Cloud

    • Japan Cloud

      For more information, see Anypoint Exchange on Control Planes.

October 2024

What’s New

  • You can now publish AsyncAPI 2.6 specifications with Avro schemas to share, discover, and reuse within your organization.

    To learn about the AsyncAPI journey, see AsyncAPI Support to Implement Event-Driven Architecture.

September 2024

What’s New

  • The Exchange Maven Facade API version 3 now supports dynamic parameters for artifactId and version fields.

    For more information, see Publishing Assets Using Maven.

June 2024

What’s New

  • You can now publish AsyncAPI 2.6 specifications to share, discover, and reuse within your organization.

    To learn about the AsyncAPI journey, see AsyncAPI Support to Implement Event-Driven Architecture.

April 2024

What’s New

App developers can now view GraphQL schemas and write, run, and test GraphQL APIs using the GraphQL console from the asset details page. For more information, see Viewing GraphQL API Schemas and Run Queries.

February 2024

What’s New

You can now see the compatible Java versions for a connector by clicking View version in the asset details page.

October 2023

What’s New

You can now find and discover assets using the Custom field filter in the enhanced search experience. For more information about the custom field filter, see Filter By Custom Fields.

July 2023

What’s New

Exchange now provides asset usage and engagement metrics for administrators and asset owners to gain insight into the consumption and user engagement of their API specification fragments and REST APIs. The usage metrics measure how many times those assets are downloaded from Exchange, imported from API Designer, imported from Anypoint Studio, and the number of dependents and contracts for the asset. The asset engagement score is a composite metric that administrators and asset owners can use to measure the usage of the assets in Exchange.

May 2023

What’s New

The assets details page lets you find specific information within the API specification and pages of an asset using the CTRL+F or the command+F keyboard shortcut. In Exchange, this enhanced shortcut overrides the native browser shortcut, which searches only for words and phrases on the current page.

April 2023

What’s New

Exchange now includes the following RPA template asset types:

  • RPA Activity templates

    Activity templates are reusable code within RPA to standardize the most used activity steps and make them available to other developers in the organization. These templates are .cawl files that are imported in the RPA Activity library for developers to use as part of their RPA processes.

  • RPA Process templates

    Templates for RPA processes are imported into RPA Builder as projects and are customizable before deploying to RPA bots. Process templates are built on common patterns for RPA to build automation faster. These templates are .crpa files that are exported from RPA Builder to share with other developers.

February 2023

What’s New

  • The enhanced search is now the default search experience for users logging into Exchange.

    Using the enhanced experience, you can:

    • Filter assets by type, organization, category, tag, and lifecycle state

    • See which API Spec properties and page text matched the search term

    • Save shortcuts to filters you have applied

    • Sort search results by relevance, name, last modified date, or rating
      For more details about the enhanced search, see Search for Assets.

      The legacy search experience is still available by clicking Back to legacy search from the Exchange landing page.

  • Exchange now supports JSON Schema and OAS 3.0 components as sub-types for the API Fragments asset type.

January 2023

What’s New

  • The documentation now uses more inclusive language.

  • The product now uses more inclusive language.

  • Exchange now includes the GraphQL API asset type.

    A GraphQL API allows a client to fetch only the object types and fields needed instead of fetching a fixed response like in a REST API.

  • A new Creator permission gives users the Asset Administrator role for the assets they create but restricts modifying assets or asset versions created by other users in the business group. For details, see Set User Access Permissions.

August 2022

What’s New

A new Conformance Status page enables API developers to see details about conformance of their validated API definitions to governance rulesets. For details, see View Conformance Status.

July 2022

What’s New

  • The search functionality has the following enhancements:

    • Improved sorting and synchronization between filters and the sidebar

    • Results display in list view when a search query is executed

    • Advanced search experience is enabled when searching for assets within the shared with me tab

April 2022

What’s New

Exchange now includes the following asset types:

  • Policy definition - Policies enforce regulations to help manage security, control traffic, and improve API adoption. Create a policy definition based on your specific business requirements and apply them to APIs to extend existing functionality or define new ones.

  • Ruleset - Rulesets are a group of rules or guidelines that define an application, for example, best practices or industry-specific standards. Add a ZIP file with multiple YAML files that describe the new ruleset.

March 2022

New Features

Exchange now supports asset lifecycle states of development, stable, and deprecated to track the progress of assets as they move through the software development lifecycle.

We intuitively redesigned the asset details page and added the following capabilities:

  • Affinity grouping - Asset information is now intuitively organized.

  • Patch versions - New Manage versions table to quickly view version details, add and delete a version, and change the lifecycle state for a version.

  • Lifecycle states - View the lifecycle state of an asset.

  • Last modified date - See when an asset was changed.

  • Collapsible metadata - Hide and expand metadata such as version, last published, categories, and tags.

September 2021

New Features

  • The Exchange API enables you to update asset metadata, including categories, custom fields, tags, and documentation pages, without needing to create a new asset version.

Fixed in This Release

  • The API is behind firewall setting persists across page refreshes and different browser sessions in the same browser.

  • Search results display correct asset names.

August 2021

New Features

  • The Exchange GraphQL API version 2 exposes the status and contractsCount properties for the API instances related to an API asset.

  • The Exchange GraphQL API version 2 exposes the apiGroupInstances property with information from the API group instances related to an API group asset.

  • The Exchange API, Exchange GraphQL API version 2, and Exchange Maven Facade API support connected application authentication, which can execute Exchange requests without sending a token by using the client application credentials of the client ID and client secret.

  • The Exchange form to publish assets has an optimized user experience.

  • Exchange supports resizing the portal sidebar to improve the readability of long API console endpoint labels.

  • The Exchange API portal includes an example curl request to add resources.

  • The API console supports options to sort endpoints alphabetically and to show full endpoint paths.

  • Exchange validates tag length.

Fixed in This Release

  • The delete version button works correctly for policy assets.

  • Selecting a section in the portal sidebar does not close API console dropdown menus.

  • Canceling changes on the asset sharing page works correctly.

  • After deleting a category, search results display the correct assets.

July 2021

New Features

  • Each asset has the optional properties contactName and contactEmail to record the name and email address of a person to contact about the asset.

  • Audit logs record creating a public portal and discarding a public portal draft.

  • Exchange API version 2, Exchange Maven Facade API, and Anypoint CLI enable you to use a single request to both create an asset and set mutable asset data including tags, categories, custom fields, and documentation pages.

Fixed in This Release

  • For users who are not logged in, public portals display a disabled request access button with a tooltip explaining that the user must log in to make a request.

  • Exchange prevents creating a category with an invalid value for the field assetTypeRestrictions.

June 2021

New Features

  • Exchange administrators and asset administrators can share an asset with a team in their organization.

  • The Exchange interface implements improved accessibility standards, including:

    • Colors with better contrast for button hover states, links to rate and review assets, and search fields

    • Typeahead styles

    • Focus states for certain menus and buttons

    • Dropdown menu styles

    • Page title field styles

  • The Anypoint CLI asset list command accepts an optional organization argument.

  • Exchange security sanitizes asset information to plain text for asset-sharing notification emails.

  • The Anypoint CLI supports managing asset portal resources such as images with the exchange asset resource commands.

Fixed in This Release

  • The View Code action correctly links to Anypoint Design Center for API assets.

  • The Open Flow action correctly links to Anypoint Flow Designer for template assets.

  • Audit logs record adding assets to and removing assets from a public portal.

  • Syntax highlighting in asset description markdown content. (EXC-3226)

  • Faster contextual navigation with clickable tags and categories in asset details page. By clicking on a tag or category, Exchange triggers a search of all of the assets that contain that tag or category. (EXC-3227)

  • Easy drag and drop image upload on Exchange’s markdown editor. (EXC-3228)

Fixed in this Release

  • The organizationId field is mandatory when publishing assets through Exchange xAPIs. Previously not sending organizationId returned a misleading 404 (Not Found) error. Now not sending organizationId returns an accurate 400 (Bad Request) error. (EXC-3168)

  • Public portals that use vanity domains to promote their company domain name can now render the API Console. API Console enables users to explore the API spec and try it out. (EXC-3143)

  • When a user goes to edit mode from a page that does not exist in the draft, Exchange now opens the home page in edit mode without an error. (EXC-2992)

  • Maven Facade now returns user-friendly and relevant error message text and code when internal services fail to validate a Mule asset. (EXC-2911)

  • Previously exceeding the rate limit for the underlying authentication service returned a misleading 401 (Unauthorized) error. Now exceeding the rate limit for the underlying authentication service returns an accurate 429 (Too Many Requests) error. (EXC-2900)

  • Exchange now prevents users from uploading compressed (zip) files whose uncompressed contents will exceed the maximum allowed size limit. Users will receive a 413 (Payload Too Large) HTTP error. (EXC-2527)

  • Allow Cyrillic text in category names. (EXC-2461)

January 2019

New Features

  • Conversion from RAML to OAS 2.0 and from OAS 2.0 to RAML in the publication process.

  • Ability to download a REST API specification in either RAML or OAS 2.0 with identification of the "Generated" specification.

  • Direct upload of RAML and RAML fragments.

  • New API console experience.

  • Consistent API specification publication user interface between Exchange and API Manager.

  • Contextual view of RAML versions of API specifications and fragments in API designer from Exchange.

Version Note

The Exchange versions have changed from version numbers to date versioning by year and month.

2.7

October 2018

New Features

  • Exchange provides root organization scope search and browse for all assets in a root organization, irrespective of which business groups users belong to. Users are no longer limited to finding assets within their own business group.

  • Vanity domain for public portals - Customers can now set their own domain name for their developer portal. This enables a more personalized and consistent branding experience, where you can use your own domain names. This also improves your search engine optimization(SEO) when your customers and users are searching for APIs that are specific to your domain. See Public Portal Vanity Domain.

  • Limits on Custom asset files - Prevents users from uploading malicious file contents as Custom types. See Create a Custom Asset.

2.2.2

September 2018

New Features

  • REST Connect combines Mule 3 and Mule 4 connectors into one Exchange asset. As a result, all previous Mule 3 and Mule 4 RAML REST API Exchange assets now appear in a single REST API Exchange asset for the RAML specification. For more information, see Converting a RAML to a Connector Using REST Connect.

2.1.0

November 2017

We are pleased to announce the general availability of the latest release of Anypoint Exchange. This release enables Anypoint Platform users to publish and share APIs with developers inside and outside of their organizations.

New Features

  • Unification of Anypoint Exchange and API portals. Now all assets can be managed and shared through a single location.

  • Ability to create public portals for any APIs in Anypoint Exchange.

  • Rich documentation automatically generated for RAML or OAS specifications.

  • Interactive API use case validation through API Notebook.

  • Mocking service, which can be used to test API calls without implementing the API.

  • Ability to register clients and request access for APIs managed by Anypoint Platform.

  • Automatic indexing of API instances and endpoints via Exchange.

  • Sharing of APIs externally using Exchange portal.

  • Customization and branding features of Exchange portal.

  • HTML support for content inserted to a Markdown editor (limitations apply).

Compatibility

Exchange 2.1.0 is compatible with Anypoint Studio version 6.4 and later.

Known Issues

  • EXC-2191: Unable to use API notebook button in the WYSIWYG mode. Click on the editor window first, and then press the Notebook button.

  • EXC-2188: API notebook creators are not able to specify the API endpoint when configuring a client. Update RAML base URI to update the endpoint used by API Notebook.

  • EXC-1510: My application page is not responsive.

2.0.0

July 29, 2017

We are pleased to announce the general availability of the latest release of Anypoint Exchange. This product enables Anypoint Platform users to publish and access Mule-related content within their own organization increasing visibility and reuse.

Compatibility

Exchange 2.0.0 is compatible with Anypoint Studio version 6.3 and later.

The new Anypoint Exchange 2 in Anypoint Platform offers a complete rework of Exchange with support for OAS and RAML 1.0 specifications, an improved user interface, a new editor supporting both Visual and Markdown text creation, and the ability to rate assets.

New Features

Anypoint Exchange lets you:

  • Store all integration assets in one place in Exchange, such as best practices, integration patterns, API fragments, API specifications, examples, templates, and connectors.

  • Enrich portal content using the Visual editor and Markdown editor.

  • Quickly upload Open API specifications (Swagger) in Exchange which automatically converts to RAML for use across the Anypoint toolset.

  • Quickly upload WSDLs (SOAP APIs) in Exchange.

  • Consume and reuse all existing MuleSoft public content in Anypoint Studio and Design Center.

  • Collaborate with API owners and designers including the ability to comment and write reviews, ask questions, and provide feedback on each asset.

  • Share an asset within a business group with users outside of the business group to drive cross business organization collaboration.

  • Auto-generate a Mule 4.0 Design Center connector (using REST Connect) for any valid API specification for use within Design Center.

  • View a list of dependencies (API Fragments) for any API specification.

  • Version any asset published to Exchange.

  • View Dependency Snippet for connectors for use in Maven, Gradle, SBT, and Ivy.

  • Publish examples and templates using Studio 6.3 and later.

Migration

Exchange 1.7 is still accessible and will remain available for 90 days (as of July 29). None of the content on this old version of Exchange has been deleted. The URL for old Exchange is now https://anypoint.mulesoft.com/exchange1/. Existing customers with content on Private Exchange can also access the old Exchange using a link available on the Exchange 2.0 site. You can migrate the content to Exchange 2.0 using migration instructions.

Known Issues and Limitations

  • EXC-1140: Unable to type anything below an image in the Visual editor. Switch to Markdown editor to continue editing.

  • EXC-1253: Visual editor is not supported for use with Internet Explorer 11. Use the Markdown editor instead.

  • Searching by tag at the user interface only works for the latest asset version.

  • Admin user cannot delete reviews created by other users.

  • Rating is not refreshed when a version is deleted.

  • Unable to deprecate an asset.

  • EXC-1522: Incorrect error message when a user without Exchange Contributor permission within a Business Group tries to create an asset.

  • EXC-1269: In Firefox, when a token is expired and user tries to publish to exchange, it throws a 403 error page. Clear cookies for Anypoint Platform and try again.

May 2016

This new version of Anypoint Exchange includes new features & functionality for addressing the viewing and publishing of artifacts across a hierarchical organization structure. Also within this version of Exchange aligns with the Anypoint Platform Styles and use of the new Nav Bar.

Features and Functionality

The following sections describe the new features in this release.

Visual Enhancements

Alignment with the Anypoint Platforms Styles and Integration with the latest Anypoint Platform Navigation Bar.

Roles for Exchange

Besides the existing Organization Owner, Contributor and Administrator Roles, a separate Viewer role was created.

New State and Flow Transition of an Artifact

To address the movement of an artifact across a hierarchical structure, Exchange now provides new states for an artifact and also specific actions to be performed on them.

Business Groups

Business Groups are being incorporated in Exchange . This feature across with the Exchange Roles and the new state transition flow of an artifact provides:

  • Ability of Central IT (maybe the root organization) to create artifacts and make them available to all Lines of Businesses (business groups)

  • Ability of Central IT to locate artifacts published in a business group and make it available to the rest of the business

  • Ability of an LOB to publish artifacts for internal (to that business group) consumption

UI and UX Improvements

New Filters and actions now support the new Business Groups, Artifacts States, and Transition Flows functionalities.

Edit Types Removal

Edit Terms only available on root Organization for Admin and Owner Organization

API Changes

Before this release, Exchange used an internal Organization ID in the API resource, but this organization ID is replaced with the Access Management Organization ID to allow Business Groups. New endpoints are being incorporated in Exchange to work with Business Groups. New permissions are applied using the Business Groups hierarchy.

Avoid Losing User Data

When a session expires, Exchange prompts for credentials and completes the action. Exchange now displays a warning when a user tries to leave the edit page if there are unsaved changes.

Removed Features

  • The object amount limitation for private tenants has been removed. The possibility to request to increase the object amount limit it’s already removed from the Exchange configuration in Anypoint Platform access management.

  • The possibility to edit types was removed, all organizations now share the same types.

  • The feature to edit terms can now only be enabled for users with Admin roles in root organizations.

Architecture Changes

  • Split UI from backend in different servers and all the related changes to fulfill this Architecture change.

  • Update Node.js version to v4.

Dec 2015

Features and Functionality

This Anypoint Exchange release includes the following new features and functionality:

  • WSDL Support: At the moment WSDL type does not have a Studio integration, however WSDLs can be added and managed via web UI.

  • Visual enhancements such as new colors for item types and UX improvements.

  • Auto-populated URI when creating new items.

  • Automatically resizable description container when editing content.

  • Firefox and Internet Explore 11 bugs fixed.

Dec 2015 Known Limitations

The version of the exchange available with the on-premises installation of the Anypoint Platform comes with an empty library of content, you must populate it with your own content.

May 2015

Features and Functionality

This Anypoint Exchange release includes the following new features and functionality:

  • Ratings: All content has a rating associated to it. Users can rate only from Exchange in Anypoint Studio (Connectors need to be installed in Studio in order to rate them). Objects have their rating displayed only when they have two ratings or more.

  • Author: Objects can have the author’s name and photo. This can be used for partners or community contributors. This section is hidden if not filled out.

  • UI Refresh: Object type indicators have been improved . Text areas and button sizes have changed to improve readability

Known Limitations

To access private content from Anypoint Studio, version 4.2.0 or newer must be used.

May 2015 Private Cloud Edition

Version: 1.4.1

This Anypoint Exchange release includes these new features and functionality:

  • Create and publish private content: Choose between a variety of content types (templates, examples, connectors, and more) to add, describe your asset, and publish it in your organization’s exchange. Only the people you choose may have access to create and publish new content.

  • Search for content: Users within your organization can find the internally published content (as well as MuleSoft’s public content), increasing reuse and avoiding redundant work. Exchange Admins can customize search filters to make internal content easier to find.

Known Issues

Accessing private content from Anypoint Studio requires version 4.2.0 or newer.

February 2015

Features and Functionality

This Anypoint Exchange release includes the following new features and functionality:

  • Create and Publish private content: Choose between a variety of content types (templates, examples, connectors, etc) to add, describe your asset and publish it in your organization’s exchange. Only the people you choose may have access to create and publish new content.

  • Search for Content: Users within your organization can find the internally published content (as well as MuleSoft’s public content), increasing the chance of reuse and avoiding redundant work. Exchange Admins can customize search filters to make internal content easier to find.

  • Seamless Anypoint Studio Integration: Access your private content seamlessly from Anypoint Studio. You can open templates or install connectors by opening Anypoint Exchange from Studio and logging into your Anypoint Platform account.

Known Limitations

To access private content from Anypoint Studio, version 4.2.0 or newer must be used.

Support

If you need help using the product, refer to the documentation for the Anypoint Exchange. If you have additional questions or want to report a problem, Contact MuleSoft.
